description: Read the result of a paid call, by its `paymentId`. Use it when `pay_service` answered `{"status":"pending"}` (the service was still working when the Router stopped waiting — a payment was attempted, the call keeps running and its outcome is not known yet), or to recover a result whose response you lost. Reading costs nothing and charges nothing. Every answer with a `state` carries `payment.status`. `state: "Pending"` — still running, call again in a few seconds. `state: "Ready"` — `status` is the service's HTTP status and `body` its response (`bodyEncoding` says whether it is parsed JSON, text, or base64). `state: "Failed"` — the call ended without a response; `failureReason` says why. That does not prove nothing was charged, so check `deliveryStatus` in `list_payments` before paying again. `{"status":"not_available"}` — nothing to return: results are kept for 24 hours for the account that paid, and only then. Do NOT call pay_service again to get a pending result: that does not return a new one. A paid body that is binary (audio, images, PDFs) or whose JSON form is larger than this server's inline limit is not inlined once the Router is confirmed to have kept the result: `bodyOmitted` comes instead, and it does NOT mean the body is empty. It gives the `contentType`, the `sizeBytes` and how to get the bytes: `contentUrl` to download with your API key (see its `instructions`), or the MCP resource `resourceUri`, also sent as a `resource_link` content block, read with the credential you send to this server. Fetching it charges nothing; do not pay again to get it. Pass `inline: true` to get such a body in the result anyway, at its full size. Requires your Nevermined API key on the Authorization header.

inline.description: Return the body in the result even when it is binary or larger than the inline limit, as base64 for binary. It can be very large (a paid audio file is hundreds of thousands of characters) and fill your context: set it only when you cannot fetch the body by `contentUrl` or `resourceUri`.
